name: demo-erp
description: What the ERP promises its subscribers: the routes it serves, the shapes it accepts, and the events it publishes. The Commerce integration vendors this file and its tests fail when the two disagree.

import.partnersNote: version 3: the ERP holds no Commerce id (no commerceCompanyId, customerGroupId, emailDomain or website); which Commerce company is which customer is the integration's key map. version 5: websiteAccountClosed is Commerce's company Active/Blocked switch, stored as the ERP's read-only website account; it never changes the ERP's own credit block (blocking), which only the ERP sets. Either one stops an order. An import from an integration built before version 5 sends the same switch as blocked, read the same way
import.stockNote: quantities per warehouse for products the ERP already has (the integration sends a product's quantity at every source on Commerce's product and stock item events); a SKU the ERP does not have is reported under stock.unknown and not created; a stock-only import does not move lastImportAt
import.seedNote: version 10: the ONE-TIME setup seed of pricing from Commerce's custom shared catalogs (Demo Builder's fill, AB-44), sent after products and partners exist. priceGroups [{code,name}] is a group per custom shared catalog; partnerGroups [{id,priceGroup}] sets each customer's price group from its catalog membership; contracts [{priceGroup,description,startingDate,lines}] is the catalog's tier prices as the group's ACTIVE price list. Silent: the prices are Commerce's already, so nothing is echoed back (no contract.changed); a seed-only import journals nothing and does not move lastImportAt

availability.note: version 11: POST products/availability — available-to-promise per line (AB-19): what is available now (on hand less committed) ships today, a shortfall after the product's lead time. The integration asks it in the placement webhook (an early signal) and again just before each part is sent, recording the answer on the order's part; it never blocks an order. Version 11 also carries the import.seed block, which landed under version 10 without a bump.

creditCheck.note: version 11: POST partners/:id/credit-check — the live credit check at placement (AB-20): can this customer carry this amount now. The same verdict the order create would reach, asked WITHOUT creating the order, so Commerce can refuse before committing (the placement webhook). status approved | held | null (no credit relationship); limit and available are null for the walk-in customer.

quote.contractNote: version 6: contractNumber names the price list whose line priced this one, or is null. version 7: most specific first, the customer's own price lists, then its price group's, then the loose contract prices and discounts, then the list price; when a price list prices a SKU for the customer, the loose ones are set aside for that SKU; the maximum discount still bounds the result

contracts.note: version 6: a customer price list (route contracts, record contract: the name the integration calls; people read price list). version 7: a list applies to one customer or to one customer price group (appliesTo), and each line has dates of its own. A list prices only when active and between its starting and ending dates, and a line only between its own too (both days included, either end open). Per customer, most specific first: its own lists, then its price group's lists for the SKU and minimum quantity its own do not price. Within one level, for one SKU and minimum quantity, the line that started later wins (its own starting date, else its list's), then the higher list number
contracts.priceGroupNote: version 7: a customer belongs to at most one price group, priceGroup on the business partner: the ERP's own, set on its screen or with PATCH partners/:id, never from the ongoing mirror import (partners). version 10: the ONE-TIME setup seed (import.seed.partnerGroups, AB-44) is the sanctioned exception — Demo Builder may set the group once at fill time from Commerce's shared-catalog membership; the ongoing mirror still never touches it
contracts.inForceNote: GET contracts/in-force answers today's prices in force for every customer with at least one line, price groups resolved in the ERP; with ?partnerId= it answers exactly that customer, lines possibly empty. version 9: the lines are what the ERP would charge the customer, by the same precedence as a quote: its own price lists, then its price group's, then its loose pricing conditions (its contract price or discount for the SKU, before its all-products discount), then the list price; the maximum discount bounds every result. A loose pricing condition counts on today's date and from its minimum quantity, as a list line does, and an all-products discount is one line per product the ERP sells. A discount stays a discountLine, so it follows the list price; a result the maximum discount cut is a discountLine at the maximum discount's percent. A product's quantity breaks are a line only where the charged price moves. version 12: a condition scoped to a sales organization (AB-46) is published per organization: the customer's lines come as one whole set per sales organization the store sells through, each tagged salesOrg, for the subscriber to write to that organization's websites; a customer with no such condition keeps one untagged set for every website
contracts.lineNote: contractNumber is the price list the line came from; appliesTo says whether that list is the customer's own (customer) or its price group's (priceGroup). version 9: a line a loose pricing condition set has contractNumber is null and appliesTo customer; a line the maximum discount cut keeps the list or condition it cut. version 12: salesOrg, when present, names the sales organization the line is for (AB-46) — the subscriber writes it to that organization's websites only, never to every website; salesOrg null is for every website (every line carries the key). A customer with any organization-scoped condition is sent one whole set per organization, all lines tagged, and no untagged line

order.spellingNote: version 10: American English on the wire. An order's status and header read canceled (was cancelled), the cancel event is raised by order.canceled (was order.cancelled), and the reason Commerce's cancel sends is Canceled in Commerce (was Cancelled in Commerce). The old spellings are refused, not accepted alongside: the ERP and the integration are deployed together. Orders and journal entries an ERP stored with the old spellings read, and are delivered, as the new ones

fromCommerce.note: A move made IN Commerce carries origin: { event, eventId? }. The ERP records it, journals it as received, and raises no outbound event for it, so Commerce is not asked to do it twice.

be-observer.sales_order_shipment_create.note: items are THAT shipment's quantities, not the whole order; stockSourceCode names the warehouse it shipped from, or is null

be-observer.sales_order_hold.note: held true puts the Commerce order On Hold (the ERP created the order and held it for credit), false takes it off (a release); reason is the ERP's credit reason, or null on a release. A reject is a cancel and travels as sales_order_cancel

be-observer.sales_order_cancel.note: reason is one of the ERP's own cancellation reasons, for the Commerce order comment

be-observer.company_contract_update.note: version 6: raised whenever a change to a price list moves a customer's prices in force today. lines is that customer's whole set (contracts.priceLine or contracts.discountLine each), so a replay is harmless; an empty list means no list price is left. version 7: a price group's list raises one for every member customer whose prices moved, and moving a customer into or out of a price group raises one for that customer. A list or line starting or ending with the calendar raises nothing: read GET contracts/in-force to follow dates. version 9: lines are the prices in force as contracts.inForceNote says, pricing conditions and the maximum discount included, and the event is also raised for each customer whose set moved when a pricing condition is created, changed or deleted (one naming no customer, such as a store-wide maximum discount, can move any customer) and when a product's list price changes on the ERP (a fixed price the maximum discount holds up moves with it). An empty list means the customer pays list price for everything. version 12: a customer with a sales-organization-scoped condition is sent one whole set per sales organization, each line tagged salesOrg (contracts.lineNote), so the subscriber writes each set to that organization's websites; the event is raised when any organization's set moved

delivery.erpId: version 4: every delivered event's object value carries erpId (a list value, the stock lines, is sent as it is), the id the integration's ERP list gives this ERP (set at deploy as ERP_ID), when the ERP was deployed with one. An event without erpId is the single ERP's. The integration matches an order message to that ERP's part and a customer message to that ERP's key-map pairs

maintenance.note: version 8: the ERP's maintenance window. POST settings/maintenance { minutes? } starts it (a whole number from 1 to 1440; 30 when absent; a second start restarts it from now), DELETE settings/maintenance ends it, and it ends by itself when the time passes. While it runs, every route of every action but the open ones answers the refusal below, reads and writes alike, and outbound events wait; a caller treats it as an ERP that is down and tries again later. health answers maintenance: null, or the window below
maintenance.healthNote: until is when the window ends (ISO 8601); message says so in the ERP's own time zone, e.g. Contoso ERP is in maintenance until 14:30 UTC.
